text:
ria: thinking loud: instead of a full proxy shim for the v2->v3 migration, what if we build a tiny negotiation header transformer that lives in the gateway? it would only touch headers and non-streaming bodies, and forward streaming unchanged.
adesh: I like header-first approach. can you list exact headers we'd mutate/observe?
ria: sketch: clients send X-Desired-API: v3 or v2. gateway adds X-Server-API: v3 and X-Compat-Reason if we rewrite. for older clients we add X-Fallback: v2-handler to signal downstream routing. also consider using HTTP trailers for debug info on streaming responses.
tom: trailers are nice but some clients/ILBs drop them. risky. keep trailers as optional debug-only.
kevin: major concern: telemetry. we need to know when rewrites happen and which tenant opted-in. metrics: compat.negotiate.count, compat.negotiate.latency_ms.p95, compat.negotiate.rewrites_per_tenant (tagged by tenant). also a trace annotation: span.set_attribute("compat.negotiated", true).
ria: agreed. operational rules: 1) header shim is off by default per-tenant. 2) small allowlist for automatic header coercions (string->json, rename x_old->xNew). 3) for streaming endpoints we only rewrite auth + headers, never payload frames.
adesh: how do we avoid double-serialization on embedding calls? payloads can be huge. header shim must not parse/modify body. good rule: only rewrite body when content-type is application/x-www-form-urlencoded or small JSON and content-length < 10KB. otherwise rewrite headers only.
tom: tests: unit for header mappings, e2e replay against recorded traffic, and a synthetic streaming test that asserts zero buffer in shim (we can assert <1KB memcopy in profile).
kevin: who owns it? sounds infra-owned but runtime needs a compatibility mapping file in repo: mappings/{tenant}.yaml with allowed rewrites. runtime must own that file and sign off on changes.
ria: deployment plan: infra builds the binary (Rust or Go), feature-flag controlled via infra config, rollout via tenant flags: stage -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. each step waits for 30m stability.
adesh: fail open vs fail closed? shim should fail-open (i.e., if shim panics, traffic routes to runtime default v3 path) to avoid global breakages. log the incident and increment compat.negotiation.failures.
kevin: add a migration dashboard card: negotiated_requests_by_tenant, rewrite_failures, p95 added latency. also add a boolean in tenant UI to enable header shim.
tom: small nit: call the header X-API-Negotiate-Via: "gateway-shim". helps clients see why negotiation happened. also include X-Compat-Trace: ticket/short-reason.
ops-bot: Scheduled: infra/negotiation-shim prototype deploy -> staging on 2024-06-03T15:30Z. Canary window reserved. :gear: 
ria: OK. I'll write a short RFC-addendum with header table, rewrite rules, and test checklist and tag runtime+infra. will also open infra ticket with proto timeline. thanks. :+1:
